newsitem.title: UK: T&G throws down job security gauntlet to car firms.
newsitem.headline: T&G throws down job security gauntlet to car firms.

text.p: The Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) on Saturday urged UK car manufacturers to tackle the issue of job security for workers just two days after U.S. car giant Ford Motor Co axed 1,300 jobs in Liverpool.
Bill Morris, union general secretary, said in a statement "It is time we started hearing a bit less about enhancing shareholder value and a lot more about enhancing employee value instead."
The union will launch a nationwide focus to "bargain for security" in 1997, he said.
The comments come as Ford workers consider whether or not to implement strike action over the job cuts at the Halewood plant.

"The industry needs to break out of the culture of short-termism - short term decisions on investment, research, training and employment...Now is the time to switch to a more long-term frequency." He said job security for the long term was the union's aim.
The T&G, one of the biggest unions in the UK, said that employers had a responsibility to invest in training to keep workers employed.
